project.name: SpendCube Phase 4 - Spend Cube and Diagnostics

summary: Phase 4 of 6. Builds the spend cube dimensional model from the canonical transactions table (populated by Phases 1-3). Implements: cube builder (aggregates by all dimensions), derived metrics computation (tail spend, maverick spend, concentration, contract coverage, WC metrics), Parquet/Excel/CSV exporter, and the data quality diagnostics module. Validation gate: cube sliceable by all core dimensions, diagnostics scorecard generates correctly from sample data.

decisions.cube_representation: Spend cube stored as a pandas DataFrame in memory and persisted as Parquet files in data/output/. Not a separate DB table — Parquet is the output format per spec. SQLite transactions table is the source of truth.
decisions.cube_granularity: Cube built at transaction level first, then aggregated views materialized. Supports arbitrary slice/dice at query time via pandas groupby.
decisions.tail_spend_definition: Bottom 80% of suppliers by count (sorted by spend desc) that contribute ≤ 20% of total spend. Configurable thresholds in config.yaml (spend_cube.tail_spend_supplier_pct=0.80, tail_spend_value_pct=0.20).
decisions.maverick_spend: Transactions where po_number is null/empty AND is_on_contract is not True. These are invoiced without a PO or contract reference.
decisions.parquet_output: Cube outputs: spend_cube.parquet (full transaction-level with all dimensions), summary_by_supplier.parquet, summary_by_category.parquet, summary_by_bu.parquet, summary_by_month.parquet. All in data/output/.
decisions.diagnostics_output: Quality scorecard as dict of {check_name: {value, status (GREEN/AMBER/RED), threshold_band}} — serialised to data/output/quality_scorecard.json and available as DataFrame.
decisions.phase_foundation: Phases 1-3 complete. transactions table in data/db/spend_cube.db has canonical supplier IDs, category assignments, all flags.

existing_tables.transactions: Full canonical schema with all fields populated by Phases 1-3: transaction_id, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_id/name, all category fields, all flags (is_credit_note, is_intercompany, is_tax_line, is_freight_line), base_amount, base_currency, payment_terms_days, business_unit, cost_centre, gl_account, etc.
existing_tables.supplier_master: canonical_supplier_id, canonical_name, parent_company_id, parent_name — populated by Phase 2

key_files: src/config.py - load_config() with spend_cube section: base_currency=AUD, tail_spend_supplier_pct=0.80, tail_spend_value_pct=0.20 (Phase 1)
patterns_to_follow: Each module independently runnable via CLI
get_transactions(engine) returns DataFrame — use this as cube source
All cube outputs idempotent — rerunning overwrites data/output/ files
Diagnostics thresholds: GREEN/AMBER/RED bands per spec quality table

userStories.title: Implement spend cube builder
userStories.description: Implement src/cube/builder.py to build the dimensional spend cube from the canonical transactions table. Loads transactions from SQLite, computes dimension columns (time dimensions, tail spend flag), and materialises pre-aggregated views as DataFrames.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/cube/builder.py — implement SpendCubeBuilder class
__init__(self, config, engine): loads config, engine

Implement build(self) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]: loads transactions via get_transactions(engine). Returns dict with keys: 'transactions' (full DataFrame), 'by_supplier' (grouped by canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_name — sum base_amount, count invoice_number, count po_number, mean payment_terms_days), 'by_category' (grouped by internal_category_l1, l2, l3 — same measures), 'by_bu' (grouped by business_unit, cost_centre), 'by_month' (grouped by year-month derived from invoice_date — format YYYY-MM), 'by_payment_terms' (grouped by payment_terms_days bucket: 0-14, 15-30, 31-45, 46-60, 60+)
Compute time dimensions on transactions DataFrame: invoice_year (int), invoice_month (str YYYY-MM), invoice_quarter (str YYYY-Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4)

Compute is_tail_spend flag: (1) sort suppliers by total spend desc, (2) compute cumulative spend %, (3) suppliers beyond top N% of suppliers (where top N% account for 80% of spend) are tail. Mark all transactions for tail suppliers as is_tail_spend=True.
Compute spend_concentration: top_10_supplier_pct, top_20_supplier_pct, top_50_supplier_pct as scalar metrics
Exclude is_intercompany=True, is_tax_line=True rows from addressable spend metrics (but keep them in full cube)
CLI: python src/cube/builder.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — builds cube, prints dimension shape summary (e.g. '10 transactions, 8 canonical suppliers, 5 categories, 3 business units')

userStories.title: Implement derived metrics computation
userStories.description: Implement src/cube/metrics.py to compute all KPI and derived metrics from the cube DataFrames. These metrics power the dashboard KPI cards and benchmarking outputs.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/cube/metrics.py — implement CubeMetrics class
__init__(self, cube: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], config): accepts the dict returned by SpendCubeBuilder.build()
Implement compute_all(self) -> dict: returns flat dict of all scalar KPIs

Compute: total_spend (sum base_amount, excluding intercompany/tax), total_suppliers (unique canonical_supplier_id count), total_invoices (unique invoice_number count), avg_transaction_size (total_spend / total_invoices), contract_coverage_pct (is_on_contract=True spend / total addressable spend), maverick_spend_pct (spend where po_number is null AND is_on_contract is not True, / total addressable spend), tail_spend_pct (is_tail_spend=True spend / total spend), tail_supplier_count
Compute payment terms metrics: weighted_avg_payment_terms (sum(base_amount * payment_terms_days) / sum(base_amount) for rows where payment_terms_days is not null), pct_missing_payment_terms

Compute concentration: hhi (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index = sum of (supplier_spend/total_spend)^2 * 10000), top_10_supplier_pct, pareto_80_supplier_count (number of suppliers accounting for 80% of spend)
Compute working_capital_opportunity(target_days: int = 45, wacc: float = 0.08) -> float: sum over top-50 suppliers of max(0, (target_days - supplier_avg_terms) / 365 * supplier_spend * wacc)
Compute data_quality_score (0-100): average of individual diagnostic scores from quality module
CLI: python src/cube/metrics.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — prints all KPIs as formatted table

userStories.title: Implement Parquet and Excel exporter
userStories.description: Implement src/cube/exporter.py to persist cube outputs as Parquet files and optionally as Excel/CSV. Creates data/output/ directory if needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/cube/exporter.py — implement CubeExporter class
__init__(self, output_dir: str = 'data/output'): creates output_dir if not exists

Implement export_parquet(self, cube: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, str]: writes each DataFrame to data/output/{key}.parquet using pyarrow engine. Returns dict of {key: file_path}. Files: transactions.parquet, by_supplier.parquet, by_category.parquet, by_bu.parquet, by_month.parquet, by_payment_terms.parquet.

Implement export_excel(self, cube: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], filename: str = 'spend_cube.xlsx') -> str: writes all cube DataFrames as separate sheets in a single Excel workbook at data/output/{filename}. Returns file path.
Implement export_csv(self, cube: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], subdir: str = 'csv') -> dict[str, str]: writes each DataFrame as CSV to data/output/csv/. Returns dict of paths.
Implement load_parquet(self, key: str) -> pd.DataFrame: loads data/output/{key}.parquet
CLI: python src/cube/exporter.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db --format parquet — builds cube and exports, prints list of files created with sizes

userStories.title: Implement data quality diagnostics module
userStories.description: Implement src/diagnostics/quality.py with all 9 diagnostic checks from the spec. Each check returns a value, status (GREEN/AMBER/RED), and threshold bands. Output as both a structured dict and a printable scorecard.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/diagnostics/quality.py — implement DataQualityDiagnostics class
__init__(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame, config): stores transactions
Implement run_all(self) -> dict[str, dict]: runs all 9 diagnostics, returns {check_name: {value, pct, status, green_threshold, amber_threshold, description, remediation}}

Implement all 9 checks as individual methods: check_missing_supplier_name() → pct rows where raw_supplier_name is null. GREEN<1%, AMBER 1-5%, RED>5%. check_uncategorised_spend() → pct spend (base_amount) where internal_category_l1 is null. GREEN<5%, AMBER 5-15%, RED>15%. check_unresolved_suppliers() → pct unique raw_supplier_names where canonical_supplier_id is null. GREEN<10%, AMBER 10-25%, RED>25%. check_missing_payment_terms() → pct spend where payment_terms_days is null. GREEN<10%, AMBER 10-30%, RED>30%. check_duplicate_invoice_risk() → pct rows where (invoice_number, base_amount) combination appears >1 time. GREEN<0.5%, AMBER 0.5-2%, RED>2%. check_negative_reversal_lines() → pct rows where base_amount < 0. INFO<3%, WARN 3-8%, ALERT>8%. check_weak_descriptions() → pct rows where raw_line_description is null OR len(words) < 5 OR raw_line_description.lower() in ('misc','miscellaneous','services','payment','invoice','charges'). GREEN<15%, AMBER 15-30%, RED>30%. check_missing_contract_linkage() → pct spend where po_number is null AND contract_id is null. GREEN<30%, AMBER 30-60%, RED>60%. check_missing_bu_cost_centre() → pct rows where business_unit is null AND cost_centre is null. GREEN<5%, AMBER 5-15%, RED>15%.
Implement generate_scorecard(self) -> str: returns formatted text scorecard with emoji indicators (✅ GREEN, ⚠️ AMBER, 🔴 RED)
Implement to_dataframe(self) -> pd.DataFrame: returns diagnostics as DataFrame for dashboard use
Implement export_json(self, path: str = 'data/output/quality_scorecard.json') -> str: saves scorecard to JSON
CLI: python src/diagnostics/quality.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — runs all checks, prints scorecard

queries.check_parquet: python -c "import pandas as pd; df=pd.read_parquet('data/output/transactions.parquet'); print(len(df), 'rows in Parquet')"

checks: Cube sliceable by supplier, category, BU, month, payment terms
Tail spend flag computed on transactions
All 9 diagnostics run without error on sample data

risks: Small sample data (10 rows): most KPIs will show edge-case values (e.g. 100% maverick spend if no PO rows). Tests should assert correct computation logic, not specific values.
Tail spend with 10 rows: with small datasets the tail spend threshold may behave unexpectedly. Use absolute count fallback: if fewer than 10 suppliers, tail = suppliers below median spend.
Parquet type compatibility: Decimal types from pydantic schema need to be cast to float64 before writing Parquet.
